observed_values.qualitative_value: GitGuardian reports 2,349 distinct secrets across 1,079 initial repositories, more than 1,100 valid credentials at analysis time, and a later phase in which 10,767 private repositories were made public exposing 82,901 secrets including 11,168 valid ones. Of 366 systems where LLM tools were targeted, 95 produced the requested inventory file. Wiz reports that AI-assisted exfiltration succeeded in under one quarter of observed cases and found fewer than 100 unique valid secrets among approximately 20,000 files attributed to the AI-assisted path in its sample.

dimensions.assessment_basis: The preserved sources establish the bounded consequence described in the Incident summary: Attackers stole an Nx npm publishing token through a GitHub Actions injection flaw and published malicious Nx package versions on 26 August 2025. The package post-install malware directly harvested credentials and sensitive files and also attempted to invoke locally configured Claude, Gemini and Amazon Q command-line tools with prompts designed to identify additional sensitive files for exfiltration. Results and stolen credentials were uploaded to public GitHub repositories. GitGuardian identified 2,349 distinct secrets in 1,079 affected repositories during the initial phase, with more than 1,100 still valid at the time of analysis, and later observed 10,767 private repositories made public, exposing 82,901 secrets including 11,168 then-valid secrets. The AI-assisted path was only one component of the attack: GitGuardian reported that only 95 of 366 targeted systems produced the requested AI-generated inventory file, and Wiz separately found substantial refusal, configuration and workspace-restriction failure rates across the invoked AI tools. Unreported downstream consequences were not inferred. Threshold applied: Large-scale or highly sensitive exposure, persistent loss of confidentiality, or substantial evidenced misuse.
The preserved Incident evidence does not report a bandable materialised financial and economic impact; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

source_records_before.relevance_note: Affected-project postmortem confirming theft of the npm publishing token, malicious package publication, approximately four hours of exposure, direct sensitive-data scanning, attempted use of local AI tools and upload of results to public GitHub repositories.

factual_basis_before: Nx directly confirms that malicious packages attempted to use local AI tools including Claude and Gemini while scanning user systems and uploading results to public GitHub repositories. GitGuardian's analysis quantifies credential and repository exposure and reports that 95 of 366 systems where LLM tools were targeted produced the requested inventory file. Wiz independently describes the malware invoking Claude, Gemini and Amazon Q with permissive command-line flags and prompt-engineering attempts, while documenting substantial refusals and execution failures. OECD.AI later indexed the s1ngularity campaign as an AI incident, but its entry is used only as discovery and registry corroboration rather than primary technical evidence. Nx also documents deletion of attacker-created branches and workflow runs during the initial token theft. Its publishing compromise occurred before local AI-tool invocation. Wiz’s later account identifies an additional repository-upload phase from 31 August involving one organisation and two accounts; this sample is not summed with GitGuardian’s broader counts. Package removal, leaked-repository removal and revocation of stolen victim credentials were separate response steps.
factual_basis_after: Nx directly confirms that malicious packages attempted to use local AI tools including Claude and Gemini while scanning user systems and uploading results to public GitHub repositories. GitGuardian's analysis quantifies credential and repository exposure and reports that 95 of 366 systems where LLM tools were targeted produced the requested inventory file. Wiz independently describes the malware invoking Claude, Gemini and Amazon Q with permissive command-line flags and prompt-engineering attempts, while documenting substantial refusals and execution failures. OECD.AI later indexed the s1ngularity campaign as an AI incident, but its entry is used only as discovery and registry corroboration rather than primary technical evidence. Nx also documents deletion of attacker-created branches and workflow runs during the initial token theft. Its publishing compromise occurred before local AI-tool invocation. Wiz’s later account identifies an additional repository-upload phase from 31 August involving one organisation and two accounts; this sample is not summed with GitGuardian’s broader counts. Package removal, leaked-repository removal and revocation of stolen victim credentials were separate response steps.
decisive_reasoning: The campaign exposed sensitive credentials and private repositories. The recorded quantities support substantial confidentiality harm. Direct malware theft also contributed: only 95 of 366 sampled AI-tool targets produced the requested inventory. The full campaign exposure is not allocated exclusively to AI-assisted discovery.
prior_blocker_resolution: The source-first review was performed. Supported minima and domain thresholds were applied; missing facts produce explicit unbanded rows or completed SU rather than an unperformed review. Original assessment and blocker remain in this audit/history.
